en: Another call for you from the highway. He had a gentle voice that made my heart flutter.
It's that regular client of yours from the highway. He said the stage was set. What did he mean?
You've been requested. Another call from the highway, perhaps? Hmm, wait a minute...
We got a call from an Onisaka-san. Oh, he's requested the chief.
Take Wada-san home, will ya? He'll give you some advice on the way.
This is a short trip. The client isn't in a hurry, so take your time and drive safely.
This client is in a rush. Get them where they want to go quickly while still driving safely.
The client sounded impatient. You'd better go as fast as you can while still being careful.
The client sounded drunk on the phone. It would be best to give him the smoothest ride possible.
The man seemed very particular on the phone. I'm not a fan of finicky men myself.
I got the feeling this client was in distress. Look after them the best as you can.
This client sounded like he really wants someone to talk to. That's another part of your job, don't forget.
This client is traveling with a child. He's interested in taxi drivers, apparently.
Dummy description.
It seemed like something's going on with this client. I hope there's no trouble.
Subtly lose sight of the car rather than follow it all way to its destination.
Learn service skills and how to talk to passengers. Encounter the Devil Killers.
The client is a businessman, but he sounded a little down. I wonder what's wrong.
The client is a young woman who seems in good spirits. Maybe she's going on a date.
The client is a young salesman. He sounded a bit depressed on the phone.
This client is a businessman. He seems a bit stressed, so see if you can cheer him up.
This client seems to enjoy talking, so make sure you let him.
This lady seemed a little prickly. I have a bad feeling about her, so watch out.
This customer had an odd way of speaking. She did speak with dignity and grace, though.
The client is a woman who sounded rather forlorn. I wonder what's the matter.
Apparently the client is a well-known politician. Watch what you say.
This client had quite the sultry voice. Don't go getting any ideas, all right?
That man sounded kind of effeminate on the phone. I've seen a fair amount of men like that at the bar.
The client was very taciturn. He seemed a little nervous as well. Be careful out there.
This client is from overseas. A great chance for some cross-cultural communication.
This time the client is an entertainer who has his own show in Osaka. Have you seen it?
The caller sounded a little rough. Maybe he's yakuza? He had someone else with him.
It's a young girl. She sounded nervous. Maybe she isn't used to taxis.
This time, you have a couple. It sounds like they're head over heels for each other.
This man sounded very tense on the phone. He has someone joining him. A couple, perhaps?
The client was chuckling into the phone. Maybe he's had some good news recently.
The client is a lady who spoke in a Kansai dialect. I guess she's not from around here.
This client sounded like a middle-aged lady. She wouldn't stop complaining on the phone.
The client is inebriated. I hope he isn't a mean drunk. Good luck, Suzuki-san!
You have to pick up two young men. They were quite rude on the phone. Kids these days...
The client didn't sound like your average businessman. I wonder what he does.

Resets status to default.
Normal wheels. You can't go wrong with the old standard.
An alternate version of the standard type. They look pretty sweet, too.
Spoke-type wheels. They really stand out.
Alternate spoke-type wheels. The blue makes them look cool.
Tornado-type wheels. Driving with these on is sure to turn heads.
Alternate tornado-type wheels. The colorful, red-accented design makes it go faster... Maybe.
Bursts of flame that display your passion for speed. Perfect for a heated race.
A Japanese design that is both glitzy and refined. This is my style.
An angel design with wings and sabers. Makes your ride look intimidating.
Kit out your ride to look like a racing car. Just the thing for competitive racers.
A cute design with a pink theme. It works for both men and women.
This is one bold design. I'm not sure Mr. Nakajima would be pleased, though.
A design featuring the idol Haruka Sawamura. It almost feels like she's riding along with me.
Taxis don't need a flashy look. A classy dark blue works best.
Make an impact with this orange coloring. It's bold but has a certain warmth to it.
Yellow attracts the most attention. Brighten up your drives.
A sky blue color that leaves onlookers feeling fresh. It's like looking up at the Okinawa skies.
A green paint job reminiscent the great outdoors. It kind of makes me feel at one with nature.
This blue scheme reminds me of the Okinawa sea. I wonder if all the kids there are doing okay.
This sophisticated pink color is popular with girls. That said, guys can get away with it these days, too.
Upgrade from level 1 to level 2.
Upgrade from level 2 to level 3.
Upgrade from level 3 to level 4.
Upgrade from level 4 to level 5.
Upgrade from level 5 to MAX level.
Standard performance you can rely on.
Designed for extended turbo use. Turbo builds faster, too, but max speed drops slightly.
Built for achieving freakishly fast speeds. Handling becomes challenging, but the driver's skill can make up for that.
Standard performance with no frills.
These have better grip than standard tires, improving acceleration and handling.
The ultimate tires for driving on public roads.
Standard performance that makes for easy driving.
A chassis built for improved acceleration and handling. Makes corners easier to take, and allows for smoother starts.
This chassis raises top speed and turbo duration, so it's perfect for speed demons. Handling suffers, however.
The standard music enabled by default. It has a Eurobeat flavor that pumps you up in a race.
A manly rock number. I love singing it at karaoke... Occasionally...
A high-tempo dance track. It was a big hit back in the day. Haruka used to sing it all the time.
The theme song for a game called Daytona USA. The iconic vocals really energize you. It's the perfect driving track.
The theme song for a game called SEGA RALLY 2006. Its funky beats will probably go down well with passengers.
The theme song for a game called Out Run. It has a good, jazzy rhythm that takes you away to the European countryside.

This is a demo of the story mode. Head to the place on the map marked in pink to move the story forward.
This is a demo of the adventure mode. You are free to explore the city.
I'd better buy a gift before I head to Tenjin Transportation. I wonder what'd work?
Tenjin Transportation is on West Gion Street if I remember right.
I should get a gift before I go apologize to Tenjin Transportation... I wouldn't want to appear rude. They're on West Gion Street.
I should send that money at the convenience store first.
I'd better hurry to where the chief is waiting. We agreed to meet at Ose Bridge.
I guess I don't have much choice. It could be a long night of drinking ahead.
It seems there are idiots like this in every town. They'll change their tune once I'm through with them.
Off to the next place with the chief, I guess. I wonder what was with those guys.
Looks like I'm going to have to beat some sense into them.
I've got work again tomorrow. I'd better head back to my apartment and get some rest.
Sosuke Komaki... I guess I'll play along.
It's getting late. Time to head back to my apartment.
I think I'll take a little look around before I head back for some sleep.

Part 1, Chapter 1 Complete
On to Part 1, Chapter 2
I've got work. I'd better show up to the office.
So the Devil Killers are out to get me, huh... Just what I needed.
I'm running late, so I should head to the office quickly.
I think we had a job come in. I'd better ask Hirakawa-san about today's bookings.
I can handle a little more work today. I'll see if Hirakawa-san has any jobs for me.
We had a pickup request come in. I guess I should talk to Hirakawa-san once I'm ready.
Daigo's missing? What exactly is going on here?

Part 1, Chapter 2 Complete
On to Part 1, Chapter 3
I have to get to Nagasu Taxi.
I think I'll walk around a bit for now.
Well, I guess I'll head home once I run out of things to do.
I'm pretty tired again today. I need an early night.
I'll go get the chief at the diner near North Chikuzengawa Street.
It sounds like Watase of the Omi Alliance is at Olivier. I need to get there before Morinaga and settle things.
Looks like I'll have to take these guys on to get some answers.
Morinaga and Aizawa are waiting for me outside Olivier. Once I'm done here, I'll go talk with them.
I have to get to the top floor somehow!
No use trying to explain. I'll have to let my fists do the talking.
I have to get to the exit quickly!

Part 1, Chapter 3 Complete
On to Part 1, Chapter 4
The Yahata Family men wear red tracksuits. I'll round some up and get them to spill Yahata's whereabouts.
I guess getting them to tell me where Yahata is won't be that easy...
Let's see if anyone else wearing a red tracksuit knows where Yahata is holed up.
They're pretty tight-lipped when it comes to their captain. At least they're doing their job.
So Yahata is in some kind of hideout. I have to take this guy down and find out where it is.
He said Yahata's hideout is about halfway down Suzukake Lane. I'd better hurry.
I have to find Yahata and talk him around.
I have to go see Nakajima-san.
If there's anything else I need to take care of, I'd better do it now.
Time to put an end to all this.

Part 1: Kazuma Kiryu Complete
On to Part 2: Taiga Saejima
My last night out. Guess I'll take a look around town.
Better do the rounds and say my goodbyes. May as well start at New Serena.
